discovery.title: Why aging stars suffer a sudden luminosity dip
discovery.summary: From a naked-eye perspective, stars are stable and predictable. Not much goes on but shining. The sun itself is fairly plain and nondescript and will shine relatively steadily for billions of years. It's considered a low-mass star compared to the most massive stars, which are rarer and contain many times its mass.
